item.title: The Sacrifice of Praise
item.description: Study-blog edition of The Sacrifice of Praise by Bill Johnson. The message explores worship as nearness to God, hosting His presence, thanksgiving, praise, costly surrender, and praising God in the middle of difficulty. Study edition: https://github.com/reubenrajan/sermon2blog/blob/main/sermons/The_Sacrifice_of_Praise_Bill_Johnson.md
item.author: Bill Johnson
item.content:encoded:
The Sacrifice of Praise

Study Blog Edition

Speaker: Bill Johnson

Source: The Sacrifice of Praise | SWBC 2026 - S2 | July 29

Introduction

Bill Johnson's message centers on worship as more than music or a church service. Worship is a lifestyle of nearness to God, awareness of His presence, surrender, thanksgiving, praise, and costly obedience.

The central call is simple: do not coast on what God has already done. Keep paying the price of a life that stays close to His presence and learns to praise Him even in difficult and unexplained circumstances.

A Ministry Directly to the Lord

Johnson begins with a lesson he learned from his father in 1971 while his father was teaching from Ezekiel. The teaching distinguished ministry in the inner court to the Lord Himself from ministry in the outer court to people.

That message led Johnson to pray, “God, I give You the rest of my life to teach me that one thing.”

He argues that the church has rightly centered itself on the Word, but Israel also camped around the presence of God. He believes the Lord is restoring the church to become a presence-oriented people, where the manifested presence of God is the central value.

John 15:7 becomes important here: abiding in Christ and allowing His words to abide in us enables us to live in cooperation with God. The goal is not merely to know words about God, but to know the person of the Word.

Hosting the Presence of God

Johnson describes learning to pause, turn his affection toward God, and become aware of the Spirit's presence before entering everyday environments. He connects this to the picture of Peter's shadow in Acts: what overshadows us is what we carry into the environment.

If worry, fear, resentment, or bitterness overshadows us, those things affect the environments we enter. If God's presence overshadows us, His presence can alter the environment.

Nothing Is Impossible Must Become a Lifestyle

The truth that nothing is impossible must move from songs and theology into daily conduct. A renewed mind changes behavior and produces a willingness to pursue what God says even when the situation looks intimidating.

Once a person has experienced supernatural supply, that person should not begin future problems from a mindset of limitation. Repentance involves a change in perspective from an inferior view of reality to a superior one.

The Kingdom Is Present

Matthew 12:28 is used to show that the kingdom of God is made manifest through the Spirit of God. Seeking the kingdom means looking for the manifestation of God's answer to the broken situation in front of us.

Worship as the Priority

Johnson describes three areas of ministry for every believer: to the Lord, to the church, and to the world. Evangelism is an overflow of worship. Isaiah 6 shows Isaiah encountering God and then responding to the call to go.

True worship does not make believers less willing to evangelize. It produces people who carry God's presence into the world. Johnson summarizes the idea with the conviction: “I owe the world an encounter with God.”

Fullness Means Overflow

“Fullness isn't measured by what you contain. It's measured by what you release.” Believers should stay filled with the Holy Spirit so that God's presence and life can overflow to others.

The Gates of Praise

Isaiah 62:10 says, “Go through, go through the gates. Prepare the way for the people. Build up, build up the highway. Take out the stones. Lift up a banner for the people.” Johnson connects this with Isaiah 60:18, where the gates are called praise.

Praise becomes a kind of highway that prepares hearts for encounter. He points to his years in Weaverville, where a community known for spiritual confusion became a worshiping community and people began to notice what God was doing.

Love for One Another

Ministry to the Lord is first, but it affects the harvest. Ministry to the church is second because Jesus said people would know His disciples by their love for one another.

Worship Begins at Home

Worship is not limited to corporate gatherings. Johnson describes turning his affection toward God as he goes to sleep and becoming conscious of the Lord's presence.

Do Not Worship Worship

Johnson's concern is not with worship music. His concern is that worship itself can become the object of worship. A person can be encouraged by excellent music and never speak directly to God. Genuine worship must remain centered on nearness to Him.

Thanksgiving, Praise, and Worship

Thanksgiving is a response to God's works. Praise is a response to God's nature. Worship is a response to God's presence.

A thankful heart is also presented as an antidote to offense. Believers should move beyond thanking God for what He does to honoring Him for who He is.

The Cost of Sacrifice

Sacrifice is more than convenience. Johnson's concern is that a mature worship culture could become comfortable and coast on what previous generations have built.

An inheritance is received freely because another person paid the price. But if we want to leave an inheritance, we must pay a price to increase and extend what we received.

Worship Is Nearness

The deepest expression of worship is not performance. It is nearness. Music can help, but the essence is nearness to God.

Honoring Someone Else's Encounter

Johnson uses the picture of hunting dogs honoring another dog's point to describe worship. When we recognize someone else who is already deeply engaged with Jesus, honoring that experience can help awaken our own awareness of God.

Keep Paying the Price

Johnson's direct charge is: “Keep paying the price.” After decades of ministry, he says he could live on the spiritual dividends of earlier years, but he does not want to coast into heaven.

Praise in the Middle of Difficulty

It is easy to give thanks when life goes well. Johnson gives a deeply personal example: when his wife died, his first response was to raise his hands and honor God as the healer.

He says her death did not change God's character. He does not claim to know why the loss happened. Instead, he says he does not need an explanation; he needs to know what to do next.

The Pearls of Praise

Revelation 21:21 describes the gates of the city as pearls. Johnson uses the formation of pearls through irritation as a picture of how costly praise is formed in loss, disappointment, and things we cannot explain.

In heaven there will be understanding. Here, believers have a unique opportunity to offer a sacrifice of praise in the middle of struggle.

Surrender, Not Striving

The sacrifices offered to God do not come from striving. They come from surrender. Great faith also comes through surrender.

The final prayer asks God to expand the believer's capacity to offer everything to Him so that He would be glorified in the earth.
